The Second Philippine Republic has 3 civilian and 1 military factories in Manila, and 1 civilian factory each in Luzon and Central Islands, leaving 16 empty slots available for additional buildings. Although that depends on how many lands can Japan occupy from the original Philippines and transfer them to the Second Philippine Republic.

The Second Philippine Republic starts off almost devoid of any resources; however, steel and chromium can be acquired via resource prospecting decisions. Just like with the industry, this can depend from Japan's advancements onto the Philippines.
The ⟦0⟧ doesn't have an army but as stated, it starts with a few division templates that inherits from the Philippines.
The ⟦0⟧ does not have a navy.
The ⟦0⟧ doesn't have an air force.
The below is ⟦0⟧ player suggested strategies for ⟦1⟧. Bear in mind, due to the dynamic nature of the game, it may unfold differently for other players.
Overview of the Second Philippine Republic

The Second Philippine Republic, despite being an in-game "nation", by Ironman choices it is almost unplayable, so the player only benefits playing the nation is by using console commands. But, another way is to release them as a puppet, wait until they get cores throughout their decisions. Although being the only playable nation without any starting existing cores, makes up for a challenge upon maintaining peace and order on the owed lands of the Philippines.
The invasion of the Philippine islands and government creation

In order to play as early as the Second Philippine Republic(PSR), is to play first as Japan and continue the war with China as soon as possible in the 1939 scenario. In this case, just invade and occupy China before preparing yourself to fight against USA for the war. Considering that the Philippines are owned as a colony by the USA. In the 1939 scenario, the player has to rush down in focuses that releases PSR faster, as in Strike the Southern Road. Therefore, acquiring the decision of 'Establish the Second Philippine Republic'. If Japan invades and annexes the Philippines, the 'Establish the Second Philippine Republic' decision releases the Philippines as the Japanese puppet.
But, if the Philippines has capitulated and is in faction with anyone else, then Japan can take the 'Establish the Second Philippine Republic' decision, thus finally releasing the PSR.

In a matter of technology, PSR also inherits whatever the Philippines or Japan gain from national focuses or by decision, if the player wishes to remain to play as Japan a little longer just to have their technologies passable for the puppet state, PSR gets them altogether. And, by decision Japan can transfer conquered Filipino lands to them for the manpower to suppress resistance and send weapons.

The ⟦0⟧ nation can be released either non aligned or fascist Japan. As it is released it starts with the political advisors, the instantly formed agency and the an unique leader. Unlike with Reorganized National Government of the Republic of China, The Second Philippine Republic doesn't have any starting national spirit or an unique national focus.

Fortunately, as stated earlier, the colony nation inherits most of the Philippines's technology, ranging from planes and artillery. Thus, opening opportunities to start and produce if needed necessary. However, being a colony state it has many draw backs. It has a decent amount of factories but some go to the colony's overlord, and some are unusable which have to be resorted to raise compliance above 70%. Therefore, independence and high compliance mean to get the great number of factories back up. Or with other means.... Although, it can core them one by one, depending how many cores does Japan pass over to PSR. But if Japan conquers them from another nation, it can transfer them to PSR.
